request.spec:
The header shows the signed-in user the due-totals of the people they watch, added up (0.00 when
watching no one).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The header shows the signed-in user the due-totals of the people they watch, added up (0.00 when
watching no one).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The header now shows the signed-in user a "Watched due" figure: the due-totals of the people they watch, added up, or `0.00` when they watch no one. All 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

This only needed a front-end change. The app already stores each user's watches and works out each person's due-total, so nothing in the stored data or on the server changed, and nothing new goes to the audit file.

- **`src/main/frontend/src/app/features/people/people-list.ts`**: a new `watchedDueTotal` adds up the due-totals of the watched people, using the same figures the people list shows. A watched person whose due-total is n/a is left out of the sum, as the existing crew total does.
- **`src/main/frontend/src/app/features/summary/header-counters.ts`**: a new `watchedDueTotal` input is shown as `data-testid="watched-due-total"`. It uses the same figure formatting as the other header totals, so German-locale users see `1.234,56`.
